_about: verification/library/: the SAT and CDCL modules, the e-graph modules, and the remaining library files outside library-a's families (vox_control.ml, vox_string_view.ml, vox_machine_semantics.ml, vox_traversal.ml, META, the flat hash table review notes). The HM, HM-to-Wasm, register allocation, regex, DFA and mode-solver demos have no files in verification/library/ at HEAD: they live in testsuite/tests/vox/. All Vox-only code, so entries have `what` only.
_sources: The code at HEAD (8479634adc): file header comments, contracts and definitions; build.sh (module list, installation); catalogue pages sat-solver.md, egraphs.md, constant-folding.md; vox_cdcl_total.md, vox_sat_boundary.md, vox_egraph_rule_handle.md; research/mastery-20260927/demos-algorithms.md sections 3.1 and 3.7, re-checked against the code.

what.short: The verified proof of Vox_sat.unsat_at, a ghost call to Vox_sat_proof.semantic_unsat_at, in the SAT solver demo.
long: `unsat_at n formula assignment` turns `Vox_sat_spec.unsatisfiable n formula`, which quantifies over assignments of length exactly `n`, into the fact that any `bool list`, of any length, falsifies the formula. The work is in `Vox_sat_proof.semantic_unsat_at`, which pads or truncates the assignment to length `n`; this file only re-exports it so that the public interface does not mention the proof module.
The result is ghost, so the whole body is erased. `sat_boundary_check.ml` checks that the `-dlambda` of `Vox_sat` makes no calls. See [the demo page](demo:sat-solver).

notes.title: The only public lemma
notes.text: A total ghost function whose refined `unit` result is the lemma. The precondition `unsatisfiable n f` is carried on the argument's type, so a client must have it in hand, typically from a `Unsat` answer of `Vox_cdcl_total.solve_complete`.

what.short: The SAT specification as let[@def] definitions: evaluation, well-sizedness, satisfiability, unsatisfiability by enumeration, and the accepted inputs.
long: The definitions behind `vox_sat_spec.mli`. Each `let[@def]` also generates an `f_def` lemma stating its equation, which proofs call explicitly; the interface states those equations, and the compiler checks that these definitions satisfy them. This is part of what a reader must trust for the SAT demo, together with `vox_sat.mli` and `vox_cdcl_total.mli`; it contains no `external` and assumes nothing.

`unsatisfiable n formula` is defined by `rejects_extensions`, a recursion that enumerates all `2^n` assignments of length `n`. It is a logical definition only: the solver never runs it, and `Vox_sat_proof.empty_unsatisfiable` proves it by induction.

notes.title: Evaluation
notes.to: eval_clause assignment clause && eval_formula assignment rest
notes.text: A variable past the end of the assignment reads as `false`. An empty clause is false and an empty formula true, so a formula containing `[]` is unsatisfiable.

notes.title: Unsatisfiability as an enumeration
notes.from: let[@def] rec rejects_extensions prefix remaining formula
notes.to: 0 <= n && valid_formula n formula && rejects_extensions [] n formula
notes.text: `rejects_extensions prefix remaining` extends `prefix` by every choice of `remaining` booleans and requires each result to falsify the formula. `unsatisfiable n formula` also requires every variable index to be below `n`.

notes.title: The accepted inputs
notes.text: At most 256 variables, 4,096 clauses and 65,536 literal occurrences, with every index in `[0, n)`. The order of the tests fixes which error a doubly bad input gets, and both solvers' contracts name it exactly.

what.short: Internal interface of the SAT proofs: resolution derivations, the private proof_result that pairs a clause with its ghost derivation, clause scanning and the learned-clause database.
long: Used by `Vox_sat`, `Vox_cdcl_total` and `Vox_cdcl_total_proof`; not installed (`build.sh` skips it when copying `.cmi` files) and not part of the reviewed surface. `derivation` is abstract. `proof_result` is `private`, so a record `{clause; proof}` can only be built by `original_result` (an input clause) and `resolve_result` (a resolvent), and every value carries `derivation_valid` for its clause.

The rest states what the solver needs about scanning a partial assignment (`scan_formula`, `scan_database`): which results mean satisfied, unit or conflict, and the facts about stable and false clauses that the termination proof uses.

notes.title: A clause with its derivation
notes.from: type proof_result : immutable_data mod total = private {
notes.text: The derivation is a ghost field, so at run time a learned clause is only its literal list. Because the type is `private`, a record literal outside `Vox_sat_proof` is rejected, so no client can pair a clause with a derivation of something else.

notes.title: From the empty clause to unsatisfiable
notes.text: The one theorem the public wrapper needs: a valid derivation of `[]` from the input clauses implies `Vox_sat_spec.unsatisfiable n formula`.

what.short: Verified resolution derivations and their soundness, the proof that a derivation of the empty clause makes a formula unsatisfiable, and clause scanning under a partial assignment.
long: A `derivation` is an input clause by index or a resolution of two derivations on a pivot. `derivation_valid` checks each premise's conclusion against the stated side clause, and `derivation_sound` proves by structural recursion that a valid derivation's conclusion holds under every assignment that satisfies the formula. `resolve_clause` deduplicates its result, which is what later bounds a learned clause to `2n` literals.

`empty_rejects_extensions` proves `rejects_extensions` over the whole `2^n` enumeration tree by induction; the tree is never executed. The scanning half (`scan_clause`, `scan_formula`, `scan_database`) is executable and is proved to classify each clause as satisfied, open, unit or conflicting. Part of the SAT demo; internal: `build.sh` does not install its `.cmi`.

notes.title: Derivations and their validity
notes.text: Only two rules: input clause and resolution. The pivot need not occur in either side clause; resolving on an absent pivot is weakening and remains sound.

notes.title: Soundness of a derivation
notes.text: Structural recursion on the derivation; the one semantic step is `resolution_sound`. Proofs call the `_def` lemmas of `derivation_valid` and `conclusion` explicitly because the checker does not unfold these definitions.

notes.title: The 2^n enumeration, by induction
notes.text: A ghost recursion with `[@@decreases remaining]` that applies `empty_result_at` at every leaf of the enumeration tree. It is erased, so the exponential tree exists only in the proof.

what.short: The verified public SAT wrappers: solve and solve_complete call the proof module and turn its Unsat, which carries a derivation, into a nullary Unsat.
long: `convert_report` is the only place where the internal answer `Unsat entry` becomes the public `Unsat`: in ghost code it calls `Vox_sat_proof.empty_unsatisfiable`, which turns the derivation of `[]` into `Vox_sat_spec.unsatisfiable n formula`. The statistics are copied field by field. Both wrappers are `total`.

`sat_boundary_check.ml` checks the `-dlambda` of this module for proof calls; ghost `n` and `formula` survive only as placeholders in the call to `convert_report`. See [the demo page](demo:sat-solver).

notes.title: Where Unsat gets its meaning
notes.text: The `ghost_` call is the whole bridge from the internal certificate to the public specification. It is erased, so the solver does no final check of its answer.

notes.title: The demo's theorem
notes.text: Never `Invalid_fuel`, never `Unknown`; `Sat` implies `check` and `Unsat` implies `unsatisfiable`. Termination is logical: time, memory and stack are not bounded.

what.short: Internal interface of the CDCL search: solve and solve_complete whose Unsat answer carries the proof_result for the empty clause.
what.long: The same entry points as `Vox_cdcl_total`, with each input error spelled out by its condition and the `Unsat` case stated through `Vox_sat_proof.derivation_valid`. It exposes none of the search invariants or the termination measure. Not installed; part of the SAT demo.

notes.title: Unsat with its certificate
notes.from: type answer = Sat of bool list | Unsat of Vox_sat_proof.proof_result | Unknown
notes.text: The certificate is a `proof_result` whose derivation field is ghost, so at run time `Unsat` carries only the (empty) clause.

notes.title: Complete search
notes.text: The contract the public wrapper converts: a valid derivation whose conclusion is `[]` on `Unsat`, and no `Unknown`.

what.short: The verified CDCL search: propagation by scanning, decisions, conflict analysis by resolution, learning, backjumping and a ghost Bigint termination measure.
long: The state is an immutable list of bindings (value, level, reason), a trail and a level; the database is a list of `proof_result`s. `propagate` scans every input and learned clause (no watched literals, restarts or deletion). `analyze` resolves the conflict clause with the reason of its latest-assigned literal until one current-level literal remains, extending the ghost derivation at each step. `search` carries fourteen invariants on the state, among them `prefix_stable`: no input or learned clause is unit under the bindings retained at any lower level.

`search` terminates by `progress_measure = count_absent * (n + 1) + unassigned`, where `count_absent` counts the literal lists of length at most `2n` over the variables below `n` that are not yet in the database. For `n = 256` it is a number of about 1,400 digits that is never computed. `prepare_learning` proves the learned clause is new: it is unit after the backjump, and `prefix_stable` says no existing clause is. Part of the SAT demo; the design is in [vox_cdcl_total.md](src:verification/library/vox_cdcl_total.md).

notes.title: Reasons and state
notes.text: A learned reason holds its database entry itself (`stored_result`, an abstract alias of `proof_result`), so no database index needs an integer bound. Input clauses are named by index, which the 4,096-clause limit keeps in range.

notes.title: The search invariant
notes.to: reason_order formula database s.learned s.bindings s.trail}) ->
notes.text: Each conjunct is re-established after propagation, decision, and learning with backjump. `reason_order` (every reason's other literals were assigned earlier) is what makes conflict analysis terminate without fuel.

notes.title: Every lower level was fully propagated
notes.from: let[@def] rec prefix_stable formula database bindings level =
notes.text: The invariant behind learning's progress: a clause that is unit after backjumping cannot already be in the input or the database.

notes.title: Conflict analysis terminates
notes.text: Each resolution step replaces the clause's latest trail literal by earlier ones, so the latest trail position among its literals drops.

notes.title: The termination measure
notes.text: A decision lowers `unassigned`. Learning lowers `count_absent` by at least one, worth `n + 1`, which outweighs the at most `n` variables backjumping unbinds.

notes.title: search decreases the measure
notes.text: A Bigint measure: the proof calls `progress_nonnegative` before each recursive call to show it stays nonnegative.

what.short: How the CDCL search works, why it terminates, and what the bounded solve promises.
what.long: Describes the accepted inputs, the search (scanning propagation, most-frequent-variable decisions set to true, resolution-based analysis), the termination measure and its argument, and the bounded `solve`, whose `Unknown` implies only `statistics.steps = fuel`. The catalogue page [sat-solver](demo:sat-solver) summarises the same argument.

notes.title: The termination argument
notes.text: The key step: after backjumping the learned clause is unit, and `prefix_stable` says no stored clause is unit there, so learning adds a clause not yet in the finite universe's database.

what.short: The SAT solver's review guide: the three public interfaces to read, what the proof modules do, and what each test checks.
what.long: The public contract is `vox_sat_spec.mli`, `vox_sat.mli` and `vox_cdcl_total.mli`; they assume nothing (no `external`) and contain no abstract predicate or name from the proof modules. The page also states the limits of the erasure check: `sat_boundary_check.ml` looks for a list of named proof helpers in the native object, which is a targeted check: it does not prove that every proof function is erased.

notes.title: What a reviewer must read
notes.to: `Vox_sequence` and `Bigint` appear only in the proofs.
notes.text: Three interfaces, using only booleans, machine integers, lists, options, results, algebraic datatypes and `===`.

notes.title: What the tests check
notes.text: The public-only client is compiled in a directory holding only the public `.cmi` files, so it cannot reach the proof modules.

what.short: The e-graph's expression language: two sorts, literals, one int and one bool input, addition, integer equality and conditionals, with sort and a total eval.
long: The first file of the e-graph's trusted specification (the reading order is in [vox_egraph_rule_handle.md](src:verification/library/vox_egraph_rule_handle.md)). It is checked code, but its definitions are what the public contracts mean, so a reviewer reads them.

`eval` is total on all expressions: `as_int` and `as_bool` coerce a value of the wrong sort to `0` or `false`. Addition is OCaml's 63-bit `+` and wraps. The e-graph's equality is derivability from the caller's rules; `eval` enters only through `Vox_egraph_interpret_wrapping.sound`.

notes.title: Expressions
notes.text: `[@@inductive]` lets the logic reason by structural induction over expressions. `Int_input` and `Bool_input` read the two fields of `env`.

notes.title: Evaluation
notes.to: Bool_value (if choose_yes then yes_value else no_value)
notes.text: Both branches of a conditional are evaluated and then chosen between, which keeps `eval` a plain total function in the logic.

what.short: Rewrite rules in the e-graph's trusted specification: patterns with sorted variables, rule validity, substitutions and instantiation.
what.long: A `rule` rewrites `lhs` to `rhs` over the variables `vars`; `t` is a list of rules numbered from 0. `rule_valid` requires both sides to have the same defined sort and every right-hand variable to occur on the left, so a match of the left side determines the right side. Nothing requires the two sides to evaluate alike: the e-graph's equality is relative to exactly these rules.

notes.title: What makes a rule valid
notes.text: `valid` is the precondition of `Vox_egraph_rule_handle.create`. The lookups return `None` or `Int_lit 0` out of range, which a valid rule with a valid substitution never reaches.

what.short: Derivations, the meaning of an Equal answer: finite proof trees of reflexivity, symmetry, transitivity, congruence and rule instances, checked against the rules.
what.long: Part of the e-graph's trusted specification. `endpoints` computes the two expressions a derivation relates. `valid rules proof` checks every step; a `Rule (i, rule, subst)` step is accepted only when rule `i` of `rules` is exactly `rule`, which is what ties a derivation to the caller's rules. `egraph_rule_rejected.ml` rejects a derivation that uses a rule absent from the list and a transitivity whose halves do not meet.

notes.title: Evidence
notes.text: A rule applies at the root of its step; congruence steps place it in a context. The type is `[@@inductive]`, so proofs about derivations are structural recursions.

notes.title: Validity
notes.text: `Trans` requires the right end of the first part to be syntactically the left end of the second. A congruence step checks only the left ends' sorts; `Vox_egraph_derivation.sort_sound` gives the right ends'.

what.short: The e-graph model exposed by the interface (a node count, a node and a class label per id) and pattern matching in it, as part of the trusted specification.
what.long: `classes graph pat bindings` lists the class labels at which `pat` matches: a variable matches only the class of its bound id, and a constructor pattern matches the class of every node with that constructor whose children lie in classes matched by the subpatterns. In the implementation the label is the id's union-find root (`Vox_egraph_match_observation.observe`).

notes.title: The graph model
notes.text: Children in `nodes` are ids. `node` and `class_id` give `None` for an id at or above `count`.

notes.title: Matching
notes.text: Repeated variables match by class equality, since each occurrence matches only its bound id's class. The list may repeat labels.

what.short: origin graph id: the expression an id stands for, rebuilt from the model's nodes; admit promises the returned id's origin is exactly the admitted expression.
what.long: Part of the e-graph's trusted specification. Each child must be a smaller id, which also makes the recursion terminate; `origin` is `None` otherwise. It does not read class labels, so merging classes leaves every origin unchanged.

notes.title: Reconstructing an expression
notes.text: Leaves give the corresponding expression; an inner node gives its constructor applied to its children's origins.

what.short: extends before after, which every public e-graph operation promises: the node count has not decreased and every existing id keeps its origin.
what.long: Part of the e-graph's trusted specification. It lets a client keep using an id returned by `admit` across later operations. It says nothing about classes, so the interface does not promise that classes equal before an operation stay equal after it.

notes.title: Preservation
notes.text: `origins` compares every id below `count` in the two graphs; `extends` instantiates it at the old count.

what.short: Closure under one rule for one assignment of its variables: if the assignment is well sorted and the left side matches at a root, so does the right side.
long: Part of the e-graph's trusted specification; `Vox_egraph_quantifier` ranges over the assignments. An assignment gives each variable an id, or a negative id for no node.
The negative case matters for a variable that occurs in neither side: without it, a variable of a sort that no node has would leave no valid assignment, and the rule would be closed vacuously.

notes.title: Typed assignments and closure at every root
notes.text: `binding_valid` requires one id per variable and a node of the variable's sort at each nonnegative id; `closed_roots` states the implication for every root below `count`.

what.short: closed_bindings: closure under one rule for every assignment of existing ids (or -1) to its variables, given only by its defining equation.
what.long: Part of the e-graph's trusted specification. The interface exports only `closed_bindings_def`; `vox_egraph_quantifier.ml` defines the function by recursion on a lexicographic measure and proves the equation, which keeps the measure out of what a reviewer must read.

notes.title: The defining equation
notes.text: The first variable ranges from `count - 1` down to 0 and then -1; each later variable restarts at the graph's node count. Sorts are checked by `C.closed_roots`.

what.short: Shows that a total function satisfying closed_bindings_def exists, by recursion on (length of the variable list, count).
what.long: Verified. `quantify` either drops the first variable and restarts `count` at the node count, or keeps the variables and lowers `count`. `closed_bindings` is defined as `quantify`, and `closed_bindings_def` restates its equation for the interface.

notes.title: A lexicographic measure
notes.text: The measure uses `Vox_egraph_quantifier_measure.length`, the length of the variable list as a Bigint.

what.short: The termination measure of Vox_egraph_quantifier.quantify: a variable list's length as a Bigint, with a proof that it is nonnegative.
what.long: Verified; a separate unit so that the trusted `vox_egraph_quantifier.mli` does not mention it.

notes.title: Length as a Bigint
notes.text: Bigint measures must be shown nonnegative at each recursive call; `nonnegative` provides that.

what.short: closed_rule and closed_rules, in the trusted specification: closure of a graph under each rule for every well-sorted assignment and every root.
what.long: For a rule with `n` variables there are `(count + 1)^n` assignments; `Vox_egraph_assignment_spec` lists them as the cases saturation checks, and `Vox_egraph_assignment_proof` shows the two agree.

notes.title: Rule closure
notes.text: `closed_rule` starts `Vox_egraph_quantifier.closed_bindings` from the empty prefix; `closed_rules` asks it of every rule in the list.

what.short: Congruence closure on pairs of nodes: two ids whose nodes have the same constructor, literals and children classes are in the same class.
what.long: Part of the e-graph's trusted specification. It is stated independently of the node signatures that rebuilding compares; `Vox_egraph_congruence_proof` shows the two agree. It is not least congruence: it does not say that classes are merged only when a rule or congruence requires it.

notes.title: Congruent nodes share a class
notes.text: `row` and `rows` are the nested loop over all pairs of ids below the node count.

what.short: The meaning of Fixed_point: the rules are valid and the graph is closed under every rule and under congruence.
what.long: Part of the e-graph's trusted specification. It describes one graph: a later `admit` or `query` can add nodes and end it.

notes.title: Fixed point
notes.text: The conjunction of `R.valid`, `C.closed_rules` and `G.closed`.

what.short: sound, in the trusted specification: a derivation valid for rules that preserve evaluation relates two expressions with equal evaluations.
what.long: The rules of an e-graph need not agree with `eval`, so an `Equal` answer says only that the two expressions are derivable from each other. `sound` takes as a premise a ghost function proving that, in `env`, both sides of every valid instance of every rule evaluate alike. `egraph_derivation.ml` discharges the premise for a concrete rule with the lemmas of `Vox_egraph_language_proof`.

notes.title: A universally quantified premise
notes.text: The premise is a total function argument, the Vox idiom for a hypothesis that holds for all arguments. An argument of type `{u : unit | p}` is a premise the caller proves by passing `()`.

what.short: The verified proof of Vox_egraph_interpret_wrapping.sound, by structural recursion on the derivation.
what.long: The caller's premise `holds` is used only at `Rule` steps. The congruence cases unfold `as_int` and `as_bool` because `eval` combines coerced values.

notes.title: Induction on the derivation
notes.text: Each case first calls `E.valid_def`, `E.left_def`, `E.right_def` and `E.endpoints_def` for the step, then recurses on its parts; only the `Rule` case uses `holds`.

what.short: The e-graph's public operations: the handle is the engine, the rules and a ghost model, refined by the engine invariant; each operation rebuilds the model and proves preservation.
what.long: Verified. Because the refinement on `t` fixes `rules` and `model` to be the store's, the ghost observations `model` and `rules` are field reads. Each operation unpacks the handle, calls the engine (`Vox_egraph_rule_hashcons` and the query, saturation and evidence modules), and proves `Preserves.extends` and exact origins with `Vox_egraph_preservation_proof` and `Vox_egraph_snapshot_proof`. In native code the handle has two runtime fields; the ghost model is erased.

notes.title: The handle and its invariant
notes.text: The refinement is the engine invariant plus `R.valid s.rules` and the two equations tying the fields to the store. A client cannot forge a handle; `egraph_boundary.ml` checks that this is rejected.

what.short: The e-graph's review guide: the thirteen specification files in reading order, exactly what Fixed_point claims, and the resource limits and search fuel.
what.long: States that the checker, SMT encoding, compiler and runtime are trusted and that the e-graph introduces no assumption or trusted primitive of its own. The resources section defines what the saturation fuel charges: generator visits, rule and assignment visits and root attempts; matching and right-hand-side admission within one attempt are not charged separately.

notes.title: Reading order
notes.text: The same thirteen files are recorded declaration by declaration in `vox_egraph_rule_handle.spec.json`.

notes.title: Limits and fuel
notes.to: occur before all rules or assignments are inspected.
notes.text: At most 512 nodes. A round is one rebuild and one exhaustive rule scan, which stops at its first change.

what.short: The e-graph's declaration inventory: the exact text and hash of every top-level declaration a reviewer must trust, and the standard-library primitives they use.
what.long: Covers the thirteen specification and interface files, with roles `semantic_definitions` and `public_contracts`, and the trusted primitives from `stdlib/iarray.mli` and `stdlib/stdlib.mli`. `egraph_boundary.ml` regenerates it from the sources and fails if it differs, so a change to the trusted surface cannot go unnoticed.

notes.title: Trusted primitives
notes.text: `Iarray.length`, `Iarray.Refined.get` and machine-integer operators, whose meaning the checker builds in.

what.short: Constructors for derivations: each builds one symmetry, transitivity, congruence or rule step and proves it valid, with its endpoints in terms of its parts'.
what.long: Verified; used by the union-find with proof edges and by the matcher. `sort_sound` shows that both ends of a valid derivation have the same defined sort, which the engine needs where it relates origins.

notes.title: Both ends have one sort
notes.text: By structural recursion on the derivation. It closes the gap left by `valid`, which checks congruence steps only on their left ends.

notes.title: A rule instance
notes.to: let proof = Rule (index, rule, subst) in
notes.text: The step from `instantiate rule.lhs subst` to `instantiate rule.rhs subst`, given that rule `index` of the list is `rule`.

what.short: Sort lemmas for pattern instantiation: a substitution of well-sorted expressions gives an instance of the pattern's sort.
what.long: Verified. `instance_sorted` is the form used for a `Rule` step: both sides of a valid rule instance have the same defined sort.

notes.title: Instances are well sorted
notes.text: Combines `instantiate_sorted` for each side with `rule_valid`'s requirement that the sides have the same sort.

what.short: Lemmas about the e-graph language: a structural equality test proved equal to ===, typed evaluation, and evaluation lemmas for common rewrite rules.
what.long: Verified. The rule lemmas (adding zero, associativity, conditionals on literal conditions, and others) are what a client uses to discharge the premise of `Vox_egraph_interpret_wrapping.sound`, as `egraph_derivation.ml` does.

notes.title: Typed evaluation
notes.text: A well-sorted expression evaluates to a value of its sort, so the coercions in `eval` never fire on well-sorted input.

what.short: The hash-cons key of an e-node: a constructor tag, a literal and up to three child ids, with the equality and hash laws the flat hash table requires.
what.long: Verified. `exact` adds that `equal` is logical equality, so a table hit identifies the stored key exactly. It is the `Key` argument of `Vox_table_implementation.Make` in `Vox_egraph_owner`.

notes.title: Equality is identity
notes.text: The table only promises lookup up to `Key.equal`; this lemma upgrades a hit to logical equality of keys.

what.short: allocated arena count: the first count cells of the hash-cons arena hold a key, and appending the next key preserves it.
what.long: Verified; an invariant of `Vox_egraph_owner`.

notes.title: Allocated prefix
notes.text: A ghost recursion on `count` over the arena's `Vox_iarray` contents.

what.short: Invariants linking the hash-cons table's slot model to the arena: every entry names a cell holding its key, and every filled cell is found by lookup.
what.long: Verified; a functor over the model of `Vox_table_map`. `valid` means a hit names a node with that key; `indexed` means a miss proves the key is new. The lemmas keep both across `put` and across any slot list with the same bindings, which is what the table's `replace` guarantees. `empty16` is the initial 16-slot table, unrolled.

notes.title: Hits are sound
notes.from: let[@def] rec (valid @ total) (slots : int M.slots @ immutable)
notes.text: Every `(key, id)` entry has `id < count` and arena cell `id` holding `key`.

notes.title: Misses are sound
notes.from: let[@def] rec (indexed @ total) (slots : int M.slots @ immutable)
notes.text: Every filled arena cell below `count` is found by lookup.

what.short: The runtime hash-cons table: an arena of keys indexed by node id and a flat hash table from key to id, with affine ghost ownership of the table's heap.
what.long: Verified. The table is `Vox_table_implementation.Make (Vox_egraph_key)`, so the e-graph inherits the flat hash table's trusted storage and SIMD contracts. Callers keep `H.at (P.own token) (T.location memo) === Some view.model`, which the table's operations require. The arena is a `Borrow_iarray.Owned_array` of 512 cells.

notes.title: The owner and its invariant
notes.from: let[@def] valid (owner : t @ local immutable total ghost forkable unyielding)
notes.text: The first `count` cells are filled, and the table and arena agree both ways (`X.valid` and `X.indexed`).

what.short: Union-find over a parent array: ordered says every parent is at most its child, so root terminates by recursion on the id and a root is its class's smallest id.
what.long: Verified; `root` also runs at run time. The lemmas cover appending an id as its own root, linking a root to a smaller one, and the roots after such a link.

notes.title: Ordered parents and roots
notes.text: An id outside the array is its own parent, so `root` is total on every int.

what.short: The runtime union-find: a 512-entry parent array and a count; union points the larger root at the smaller, with no path compression or ranks.
what.long: Verified. Linking to the smaller root keeps `S.ordered`, the invariant that makes `root` terminate without a separate measure. `union_semantics` gives the root of every id after a union.

notes.title: Union
notes.from: let union : (state : {s : t | valid s}) @ immutable ->
notes.text: `Vox_iarray.updated` copies the parent array, so each union costs a 512-element copy.

what.short: The proof-producing part of the union-find, all ghost: each non-root id has an edge, a valid derivation from its origin to its parent's origin.
what.long: Verified. `explain` follows parents to the root and chains the edges with `Trans`, so two ids with the same root get a derivation between their origins (`same_class_evidence`). The frame lemmas show that appending an id and linking a root to a smaller one keep `valid_edges`.

notes.title: Edges carry derivations
notes.text: A root has no edge; any other id's edge is valid for the rules and relates its origin to its parent's.

notes.title: Evidence for a class
notes.text: Two explanations to the common root, one reversed with `symmetric`, joined by `transitive`.

what.short: The union-find with proof edges: Vox_egraph_union at run time plus the ghost rules, origins and edges; a merge must supply a derivation.
what.long: Verified. `merge` takes a derivation from the larger root's origin to the smaller root's and stores it as the loser's edge; `merge_nodes` takes one between any two ids and converts it with `root_proof`. So any two ids of a class have a derivation between their origins (`same_evidence`). Only `union` remains at run time.

notes.title: Ghost fields
notes.text: `rules`, `origins` and `edges` are ghost; the initial 512-entry arrays come from `Vox_egraph_ghost_arrays`.

notes.title: A merge needs evidence
notes.from: let merge : (state : {s : t | valid s}) @ immutable ->
notes.text: The ghost `proof` argument must be valid for the rules and relate the two roots' origins in the direction of the link.

what.short: The initial ghost arrays of Vox_egraph_rule_union: 512 placeholder origins and 512 empty edges, both erased.
what.long: Verified; the length is stated in the result type. `egraph_ghost_arrays_erasure.ml` checks that neither array is built at run time.

notes.title: Placeholder origins
notes.text: `Int_input` stands in for ids not yet allocated; admission overwrites it at the fresh id.

what.short: preserved before after count: two ghost origin arrays agree below count; every mutating operation returns it for the old count.
what.long: Verified. Admission writes origins only at fresh ids and merges never write them. The lemmas compose, weaken and read the relation; `Vox_egraph_preservation_proof` turns it into the public `extends`.

notes.title: Agreement below a count
notes.text: Recursion on `count` over `Vox_iarray.at`.

what.short: E-nodes with children as ids: injective keys, canonical forms and signatures for congruence, origins, typing and frame lemmas.
what.long: Verified. `canonical` replaces the children by their union-find roots and `signature` is the key of that; equal signatures are how rebuilding finds congruent nodes. `origin` builds a node's expression from its children's ghost origins. The frame lemmas show that writing above a node's children changes neither its origin nor its typing.

notes.title: Signatures
notes.text: Two nodes are congruent in the model exactly when their signatures are equal (`Vox_egraph_congruence_proof.signature`).

what.short: The e-graph store without the hash-cons index: the proof-producing union-find, a node and a sort per id, all 512-entry immutable arrays.
what.long: Verified. The invariant `valid` asks, for every id below the count, that the node's children are smaller ids of the right sorts, that the recorded sort is the node's, and that the ghost origin is the node applied to its children's origins (`node_ok`). `add` writes only at the next id. The module also builds the derivations that justify congruence merges and defines the closure state that rebuilding establishes.

notes.title: Fields
notes.text: Nodes and sorts are runtime arrays updated by copying; the origins live in the ghost part of `semantic`.

notes.title: The store invariant
notes.text: Both arrays have 512 entries, and `nodes_valid` asks `node_ok` at every id below the count; children below their parent is what makes `Vox_egraph_snapshot_spec.origin` agree with the recorded origins.

what.short: The e-graph engine: the hash-cons table and the store together, with add, admit_expr, merge, pairwise rebuild and extract.
long: Verified. `matching` says the arena holds the key of each stored node, so a table hit on `N.key node` names an id whose node is `node` (`lookup_origin`). Nodes are hash-consed with their children as given; nodes congruent up to class are merged by `rebuild`, a pass over all pairs of nodes.
No operation changes the origin of an existing id. `rebuild` is `total` and bounded by its pass count; a pass that does not finish its pair scan returns `Work_limit`.

notes.title: The engine invariant
notes.text: The conjunction that the functions here, and the modules built on them, also state inline in their contracts.

notes.title: Rebuild
notes.text: `Stable_pass` gives `V.closed_fuel` over all pairs, which `Vox_egraph_congruence_proof` turns into congruence closure of the model.

what.short: Turns a complete rebuild pass into the trusted congruence closure of the model, by relating node signatures to the spec's same_node.
what.long: Verified. `signature` shows that two nodes are congruent in the model exactly when their signatures are equal, `scan_at` reads one pair out of `closed_fuel`, and `row` and `rows` follow the nested loop of `Vox_egraph_congruence_spec`.

notes.title: From the rebuild state to the spec
notes.text: The entry point used by saturation after each complete rebuild.

what.short: The model the public interface exposes: the store's node array with, at each id, its union-find root as class label.
what.long: Verified. The lemmas read the model's class labels, class equality and nodes back as roots and array reads. The model is ghost; `labels` is never computed at run time.

notes.title: Observation
notes.text: A class label is a union-find root, so two ids are in the same model class exactly when their roots are equal.

what.short: The executable matcher: each function is proved equal to its counterpart in the trusted Vox_egraph_match_spec on the observed model.
what.long: Verified. It reads nodes and roots directly without building the model. `classes` computes, bottom-up over the pattern, the class labels where the pattern matches, scanning every node once per constructor; `find_layer` finds a node of a given class that realises one constructor.

notes.title: Matching by scanning
notes.text: The model appears only as a ghost `O.observe nodes parents count` in the contract.

what.short: The cost model of the bounded matcher, a diagnostic separate from the saturation fuel: the exact units matching a pattern charges.
what.long: Verified definitions used by `Vox_egraph_match_bounded`.

notes.title: Work
notes.text: A variable costs one unit; each constructor costs `1 + count` plus the work of its subpatterns, one pass over the nodes per constructor.

what.short: A bounded matcher with an exact cost: Exhausted exactly when fuel is below the budget spec's work, and otherwise the trusted matcher's classes.
what.long: Verified. A diagnostic exercised by `egraph_match_observation.ml`; saturation does not use it.

notes.title: Exact cost
notes.text: On success the remaining fuel is exactly `fuel - work`.

what.short: Introduction for the trusted matches: a node in root's class with the pattern's constructor and children in the subpatterns' classes makes the pattern match.
what.long: Verified. `first`, `second` and `third` are the child class lists; `collect_contains` shows that the node's class is collected.

notes.title: Introducing a match
notes.text: Used when the rewriter proves that a newly admitted right-hand side matches.

what.short: Ways to establish a match in a store's model: by constructor, by a bound variable, and by moving a match to another id of the same class.
what.long: Verified; the store-level counterpart of `Vox_egraph_match_intro`.

notes.title: Matches follow classes
notes.text: A pattern matches at a class, so any two ids of that class match alike.

what.short: present: every variable of a pattern is bound to an id with a class; a match implies it, and rule validity carries it from the left side to the right.
what.long: Verified. Together `matched` and `transfer` show that the right-hand side of a matched rule can be admitted.

notes.title: From left to right
notes.text: Uses the rule validity condition that every right-hand variable occurs on the left.

what.short: Checks a list of bindings against the variables' sorts and builds the corresponding ghost substitution.
what.long: Verified. `accepts` requires every id to be below the node count and every bound id's origin to have its variable's sort. `build` decides this at run time from the `sorts` array and, on success, returns a substitution valid for the variables that `agrees` with the bindings; a variable bound to -1 gets a default expression of its sort.

notes.title: Accepted bindings
notes.text: `Vox_egraph_saturation_proof` shows this executable check coincides with the trusted `binding_valid` on the model.

what.short: Derivations from matches: derive turns a match of a pattern at an id into a valid derivation from the id's origin to the pattern's instance.
what.long: Verified. `view` is the model of a store. `agrees origins bindings subst` says the substitution names the origin of every bound id. `derive` recurses on the pattern: it picks the node of the root's class that realises the top constructor (`witness`), derives its children, applies the congruence step and prepends the class derivation from the root to that node (`same`).

notes.title: The derivation for a match
notes.text: This, followed by the `Rule` step, is the evidence a rewrite stores when it merges the right-hand side into the matched class.

what.short: The implementation of same_class: compares union-find roots and, when they agree, returns the erased derivation from Vox_egraph_match_evidence.same.
what.long: Verified and `total`. The ghost block relates the answer to the model: `Q.same` on the model is equality of roots, and the model origin of each id is its ghost origin.

notes.title: Exact class comparison
notes.to: let proof = ghost_ (if equal then Some (P.same state a b ()) else None) in
notes.text: The runtime work is two `root` calls and a comparison; the proof is built only in ghost code.

what.short: For a valid store, the trusted origin of an id in the model is the ghost origin recorded when the id was admitted.
what.long: Verified, by recursion on the id; the store invariant puts every child below its parent.

notes.title: Recorded origins are exact
notes.from: let rec (origin @ total) : (state : V.t) @ immutable -> (id : int) ->
notes.text: This is how `admit` proves the returned id stands for exactly the admitted expression.

what.short: Proves the trusted extends for two stores' models from preserved on their ghost origin arrays, and exports preserved_origin.
what.long: Verified. `origins` goes id by id through `Vox_egraph_snapshot_proof.origin`. `preserved_origin`, which reads one id's origin out of `extends`, is re-exported as `Vox_egraph_rule_handle.preserved_origin`.

notes.title: extends from preserved
notes.text: Every mutating operation returns `preserved` for the old count; this lemma turns it into the public promise.

what.short: Facts about bindings that survive admitting new nodes, for admitting a right-hand side one part after another.
what.long: Verified. `bounded` (every id below a count) and `available` (every variable of a pattern bound to an existing id) only weaken as the count grows; `preserve` keeps `agrees` across a preserved origin array. `rhs_admissible` collects the premises of `Vox_egraph_pattern_admit.admit` for a matched rule's right-hand side.

notes.title: Premises for admitting the right side
notes.text: Combines the match, rule validity and the accepted bindings.

what.short: Admits the instance of a pattern under bindings: a variable is looked up, a constructor is hash-consed bottom-up; the result's origin is the instantiated pattern.
what.long: Verified; used by `Vox_egraph_rule_rewrite` to add a rule's right-hand side. If no node was added, the returned id already matches the pattern under the bindings in the unchanged graph, which is what lets an application that changes nothing establish closure at its root.

notes.title: Admission and its contract
notes.text: The result's origin is `R.instantiate pat subst` for a ghost `subst` that agrees with the bindings.

what.short: One rule application under given bindings at a given root: checks the bindings, matches the left side, and admits and merges the right side with a derivation.
what.long: Verified. If the right-hand side already matches at the root, nothing changes. Otherwise the merge is justified by the erased derivation from the root's origin to the left-hand instance (`P.derive`) followed by the `Rule` step. When nothing changes, the contract shows the rule holds at this root: the bindings are rejected, the left side does not match, or the right side matches.

notes.title: One application
notes.text: The postcondition's no-change case is the per-root, per-assignment closure fact that `Vox_egraph_rule_scan` sums up.

what.short: Applies one rule instance from an explicit substitution: admits both sides as expressions and merges them with an erased Rule derivation.
what.long: Verified. Saturation does not use it (it matches in the graph through `Vox_egraph_rule_rewrite`); the rule tests exercise it.

notes.title: Instance application
notes.text: `Invalid_rule` and `Node_limit` are the two ways it can decline.

what.short: The candidate assignments saturation enumerates for one rule, as an explicit list of (count + 1)^n cases, and closure over them.
what.long: Verified definitions. Entries run over the ids `count - 1` down to 0 and then -1; sorts are not filtered here. `Vox_egraph_assignment_proof` shows that `closed_cases` over this enumeration equals the trusted `closed_rule`.

notes.title: Every assignment
notes.text: Built from `choices` and `prepend`, which the executable `Vox_egraph_assignments` mirrors with fuel.

what.short: Proves the trusted closure of one rule equal to closure over the explicit enumeration of assignments.
what.long: Verified. The quantifier accumulates a prefix with `snoc` while the enumeration prepends ids to suffixes, so the induction is over `closed_prefixed`, which puts a fixed prefix in front of every case.

notes.title: The two quantifications agree
notes.text: Used by `Vox_egraph_rule_scan` to conclude `closed_rule` from a scan that changed nothing.

what.short: Executable, fuel-charged versions of the assignment enumeration; each returns Exhausted or the spec's cases with strictly less fuel.
what.long: Verified. This is the assignment-generator part of the saturation fuel described in `vox_egraph_rule_handle.md`: each call charges one unit.

notes.title: Enumeration with fuel
notes.text: On success the result is exactly `C.assignments count vars`.

what.short: The search for one rule: every assignment, every id as the root of a match, stopping at the first application that changes the graph.
what.long: Verified. If the search finishes without a change, the store is unchanged and every attempt showed the rule closed at its root and assignment, which adds up to `Vox_egraph_saturation_spec.closed_rule`. Each case, root attempt and enumeration step costs one unit of fuel. For a rule with `n` variables one search tries up to `(count + 1)^n × count` matches.

notes.title: Every root
notes.text: Here a root is the id at which the left side is matched; it need not be a union-find root. Ids are tried from `count - 1` down to 0.

notes.title: One rule
notes.to: let count = (let view = borrow_ state in view.owner.count) in
notes.text: The `Stable` postcondition is `S.closed_rule` on the unchanged model.

what.short: A cursor into the rule list: drop rules i is the list without its first i rules, with lookup and advance lemmas.
what.long: Verified; used by `Vox_egraph_rules_scan`. The bound on `index` keeps `index + 1` from overflowing.

notes.title: Suffixes of the rule list
notes.text: `lookup` shows the head of the suffix is `R.lookup_rule rules i`.

what.short: One pass of the rule search over every rule, stopping at the first result other than Stable.
what.long: Verified. `Stable` means the store did not change and every rule in `todo = Cursor.drop rules index` is closed on it. The fuel bound `fuel <= max_int - index` keeps `index + 1` from overflowing, since each rule costs a unit.

notes.title: All rules
notes.text: At the end of the list `todo` is empty, so `Stable` gives `closed_rules` for all of them.

what.short: The saturation loop: each round rebuilds and then runs one pass of the rule search; a Stable pass returns Fixed_point.
what.long: Verified. A pass that changes the graph starts the next round, so a round applies at most one rewrite. Search fuel carries over between rounds; rebuilding does not use it. `Fixed_point` is proved from the rebuild's congruence closure and the scan's rule closure together.

notes.title: Rounds
notes.text: The postcondition for `Fixed_point` is `F.fixed` of the model; the other statuses say only which limit was hit.

what.short: On a valid store, the trusted typing condition binding_valid on the model coincides with the executable check Vox_egraph_match_subst.accepts.
what.long: Verified; used by `Vox_egraph_rule_scan`.

notes.title: Executable check equals spec
notes.text: An equality of booleans, so both directions come at once.

what.short: The implementation of query: admits both expressions and compares their classes, without rebuilding or saturating.
what.long: Verified. An `Equal` answer carries the derivation from `Vox_egraph_rule_union.same_evidence`; since each admitted id has the admitted expression as its origin, the derivation's endpoints are the two expressions. A failing query may still have added nodes for well-sorted subexpressions.

notes.title: Query
notes.text: `Not_proved` is returned whenever the classes differ, which is why it carries no information.

what.short: A byte-level control-group API: a trusted SIMD matching builtin with a bounds-checked wrapper, the 7-bit fingerprint, and clearing a mask's lowest bit.
long: `match16_valid` is an `external` marked `[@@builtin]`, compiled inline by `backend/cmm_builtins.ml` (NEON, SSE2 or scalar) with the C stub in `runtime/vox_control.c`. Its assumed contract is only the result type `mask`, an int in `[0, 65535]`; which lanes are set is stated in prose in `vox_control.mli` and tested by `control_group.ml`. `match16` checks the offset and byte and raises `Invalid_argument` otherwise. `fingerprint` and `clear_first` are verified.

No verified library module calls it. The flat hash table matches through its own externals, `Vox_table_storage.match16` and `match16_empty`, whose stubs in `runtime/pref.c` call the same C matching code on the table's control bytes and whose lane semantics are part of `Vox_table_storage`'s contract.

notes.title: The trusted builtin
notes.text: `[@@noalloc] [@@builtin] [@@no_effects]`: the compiler emits the match inline. The refinement on `mask` bounds the result and says nothing about which bytes matched.

notes.title: Clearing the lowest lane
notes.text: Proved to strictly decrease a nonzero mask, so a loop that clears one matching lane at a time terminates.

what.short: Three trusted externals that view a string as a ghost char iarray: contents, and length and unchecked get specified against it.
what.long: `contents` is ghost and never runs; `length` is `%string_length` and `get` is `%string_unsafe_get`, whose index precondition is proved by the caller. The contracts are assumed. Used by the LZ4 string codecs; compiled at `-O3` in native code so that client functors are specialised.

notes.title: Unchecked reads with a proved index
notes.text: The result is tied to `Vox_iarray.at (contents source) index`, so a proof about the ghost view speaks about the bytes read.

what.short: Proofs that 63-bit int addition, subtraction and comparison agree with Bigint arithmetic followed by signed wrap-around.
what.long: Verified: each lemma's body is `ghost_ (())` or a single `signed_def` call, and the SMT solver proves the rest from Vox's encoding of `int` operations. Used by the [constant-folding](demo:constant-folding) demo, whose evaluator uses wrapping `+`. Not in `build.sh`'s module list.

notes.title: Wrap-around
notes.text: Reduces a Bigint into `[-2^62, 2^62)`, the range of a 63-bit int.

notes.title: Addition wraps
notes.text: The lemma follows from the verifier's own encoding of `+` on `int`; this file makes that encoding available as a stated fact.

what.short: Experimental checked implementations of map and fold whose callbacks may be partial, specified by total relations and fold invariants.
what.long: Checked by `library_build.ml` and exercised by `collection_functions.ml`; not in `build.sh`, so not installed. The design comparison is in [hof-idioms.md](src:design-docs/hof-idioms.md).

notes.title: map by a relation
notes.text: The callback need not be total; its result is refined by `r x y`, and the output list is related to the input by `map_rel r`.

what.short: The findlib description of the installed library: the archives vox_borrow.cma and vox_borrow.cmxa.
what.long: `build.sh` copies it to `lib/ocaml/vox`. The archive holds every module in `build.sh`'s list; the `.cmi` files of `vox_sat_proof` and `vox_cdcl_total_proof` are not installed, and RSA, diff, the e-graph modules, `vox_machine_semantics` and `vox_traversal` are not in the list (tests compile them).

notes.title: Archives
notes.text: One archive for the whole library.

what.short: The flat hash table's ordered review surface: the files to read, the trusted semantics and limits, and the proof boundary and its evidence.
what.long: Lists, in reading order, the interfaces and model files a reviewer must accept (`stdlib/bigint.mli`, `pref.mli`, `ghost_pref.mli`, parts of `vox_sequence.mli`, `vox_table_model.ml`, `vox_table_bits.ml`, `vox_table_storage.mli`, `vox_verified_flat_hashtbl.mli`), then the trusted semantics and the tests. Its baseline line names an earlier PR head; the catalogue page [flat-hash-table](demo:flat-hash-table) is the current summary.

notes.title: Reading order
notes.text: Each entry says which part of a shared interface the table's contract depends on.

what.short: A dated working note (25 September 2026) on simplifying the flat hash table's specification and code, with a later amendment.
what.long: Records the move to a finite binding model, the separation of existing-key replacement from `insert_absent_hashed`, and a rejected combined-traversal experiment. Its first section is superseded by the amendment of 26 September: `Map.t` is now abstract, with `empty`, `lookup`, `put`, `erase`, `same` and `count` and their laws. Read `vox_verified_flat_hashtbl.mli` for the current interface.

notes.title: Superseded section
notes.text: The list model moved to `Vox_table_bindings.Make(Key).Assoc`, below the public interface.
